external_entities.name: Supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal with vendor-issued credentials.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

external_entities.name: Vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the SaaS portal, issues supplier credentials, and pushes nightly supplier data extracts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

external_entities.name: Category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

processes.name: Supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload compliance paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.

processes.name: Supplier master service
processes.description: A service in our cloud account that loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: Vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor's platform where supplier compliance documents remain.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: Landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in our cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is; the description also says the nightly extract was said to be encrypted end to end.

data_stores.name: Supplier database
data_stores.description: The database in our cloud account into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: A supplier uploads compliance paperwork and contact details through the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff.

data_flows.name: review paperwork
data_flows.description: A category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it in the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded compliance paperwork and approval or rejection decisions.

data_flows.name: store documents
data_flows.description: The portal stores supplier compliance documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The description says: "We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end." The runbook says: "The file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is." These claims conflict, so encryption in transit is unknown.

data_flows.name: load extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes the extracted supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database
data_flows.data_description: Supplier records from the nightly extract.

trust_boundaries.name: Vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting environment for the SaaS portal and vendor platform.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: Our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: Our cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier and category manager actors are modeled as human external entities because the text describes people signing in, uploading, reviewing, approving, and rejecting paperwork.
assumptions.basis: Suppliers sign in and upload paperwork through the portal.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier compliance records are confidential because they include contact details for staff and commercially relevant compliance paperwork.
assumptions.basis: The store contains insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket contents are confidential because it receives supplier data extracts.
assumptions.basis: The landing bucket receives a supplier data extract.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database contents are confidential because it contains supplier records and contact details.
assumptions.basis: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the database.
